DELIBERATELY NOT INGESTED: BPHS's longevity and maraka material (ch.19, ch.43, ch.44, ch.9-10 arishta, and the 2nd/7th/8th-lord dasha rows of ch.48 that read 'possibility of death'). Longevity is a refer-out under CLAUDE.md, so those rules must not be retrievable by a domain agent at all. Their absence here is a decision, not an oversight — see docs/health_kb_bphs_6th_house.md. Marriage rules added 2026-08-12 from BPHS ch.18 and ch.24.73-84. THREE CLASSES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT. (1) Rules whose only content is a spouse's obedience or the native's control over them (ch.24.76, ch.24.82) — there is no neutral rule inside them to keep. (2) The passages describing a partner's body and sexual acts (ch.18.9 and surrounding notes). (3) Timing of a spouse's death (ch.18.3, 18.35-39, 18.42), which is longevity and refers out. The chapter is written throughout for a male native with a wife; that gender is the period reader's assumption and not a claim the chart makes, so statements here say spouse or partner. See docs/marriage_kb_bphs_7th_house.md.

Children and foreign rules added 2026-08-12. CHILDREN: BPHS ch.16 required more content exclusion than any prior chapter — legitimacy/paternity claims (16.14, 16.15) excluded outright, no neutral core; the sex-of-children rule (16.13) excluded on real-world-harm grounds (son-preference bias), a stricter bar than gendered-language cleanup alone; child-death timing (16.21-23) is gated_death; the exact-count-of-children block (16.24-32) excluded as an unservable deterministic claim with embedded death timing, not picked apart row by row. See docs/children_kb_bphs_5th_house.md. FOREIGN: honestly thin. BPHS's 12th-lord series (ch.24.134-144) and the 3rd/9th house chapters were checked in full and contain no explicit foreign-travel statement in this translation; only ch.23.11-12 speak to it directly. Saravali (the earlier standing candidate) was checked directly and found not to reach house-effect chapters in the volume we hold (Vol I runs chapters 1-26, fundamentals only) -- Phaladeepika's Adhyayas V/X/XII/XX map onto career/marriage/children/dasha, which is why it was used instead. Adds a new career technique (navamsa of the 10th lord), cross-verifies three marriage and three children claims previously single-source, adds dasha-timing rules for both, and independently corroborates the dasha dignity-over-nature principle and the maraka-lords-give-gain caveat. See docs/phaladeepika_crosscheck.md for the full reasoning, including the exclusions -- this pass found the single most severe content problem in the corpus so far: Adhyaya XII attributes childlessness to sin in a previous birth and prescribes ritual atonement per planet. Excluded outright, along with a second, unhedged version of BPHS's spouse-death timing problem, an exact-count-of-wives block mirroring the exact-count-of-children exclusion, and a technique for predicting a future spouse's own birth sign -- excluded as an enabler of astrological compatibility-gatekeeping.

Material previously classed gated_medical in ch.17 (facial disease, the leprosy verses, the Sun/Ketu clauses of the general-disease block, and the timing-of-illness block) is reframed as body-system or life-stage cautions -- naming an area worth checking, never a specific disease, never a specific age. references.statement: The 10th bhava governs livelihood, rank, honour and karma; its lord's strength and placement set the career's trajectory.
The dashamsha (D10) refines the 10th-house promise: planets strong in D10 mark the arenas where public action succeeds.
Amala Yoga — a natural benefic in the 10th from Lagna or from Moon — is classically read as steady professional reputation that holds up over time, distinct from raw career success or wealth.
The 7th bhava and its lord, together with Venus as kalatra karaka, govern the spouse and the quality of the union; the navamsha (D9) confirms or withholds the rashi promise.

Manglik (Kuja) placements are classically read as a factor affecting marital harmony and timing, always alongside the classical cancellation rules (Mars in its own or exalted sign, Jupiter's aspect on Mars, Mars-Moon conjunction) — a flag to weigh, never a standalone verdict against marriage.

Venus as the natural karaka for marriage and relationship harmony is read alongside the 7th lord and house — a well-placed 7th house with an afflicted Venus (or vice versa) is a common classical pattern for a mixed marital picture, not a simple pass/fail.
The 6th bhava carries disease, debt and enemies together; afflictions to the 6th and its lord activate all three significations and must be separated by karaka and context.

The Lagna (1st bhava) and its lord govern overall vitality and constitution; a strong, undamaged Lagna lord is classically read as a baseline of resilience that other houses' afflictions play out against.

The 6th bhava and its lord are the primary reference for chronic and recurring illness; Saturn's involvement there is classically associated with slow-onset or long-duration conditions, Mars' involvement with acute, sudden onset — read as tendency, never as diagnosis.
The Atmakaraka (highest-degree graha) shows the soul's desire; its navamsha position (Karakamsha) frames the spiritual path and final direction.

The 12th bhava governs moksha (liberation), renunciation, and detachment from worldly bonds; the 9th governs dharma and guru connection — classical texts read the two together as part of the 'moksha trikona' axis with the 4th and 8th.
The Vimshamsha (D20) is examined specifically for spiritual practice (sadhana), devotion, and the nature of one's religious or ritual inclination — a finer lens than the 9th/12th houses alone.
The 2nd bhava shows accumulated wealth and family resources; the 11th shows income and gains. Dhana Yoga forms when the lords of these two houses associate, favouring material prosperity.

Dhana Yoga arises when the lords of the wealth houses (2nd, 5th, 9th, 11th) associate by conjunction, mutual aspect, or exchange; the association's strength and the lords' dignity set how much of the promise materializes.
Chandra-Mangal Yoga (Moon and Mars conjoined or opposed) is classically read as a driver of enterprising wealth-building — an active, self-made financial temperament rather than inherited ease.

The 4th bhava governs basic schooling and foundational learning; the 5th governs higher intellect, specialized study, and academic merit. The Chaturvimshamsha (D24) refines which field of learning and how much of the promise the native actually pursues.
Saraswati Yoga — Jupiter, Venus and Mercury each well-placed from Lagna with Jupiter strong — is the classical marker for articulate, wide-ranging learning and refined intellect.

Mercury's strength and dignity are read as one of the most consistent indicators of ease in formal education; an afflicted or debilitated Mercury is a common thread in charts with schooling breaks or difficulty, though never a standalone verdict.

The 5th bhava and its lord, together with Jupiter as the naisargika putrakaraka (natural significator of children), govern progeny — timing, number, and relationship; the Saptamsha (D7) is examined specifically for children's promise.

In the Jaimini scheme, the Putrakaraka (PK, the chara karaka for children) adds a second, planet-specific lens on progeny alongside the fixed 5th-house/Jupiter reading — the two should be read together, not substituted for each other.

Afflictions to the 5th house or its lord are read as timing/ease factors for conceiving and raising children, not as a fixed verdict — classical texts pair every affliction with cancellation and remedial factors.
The 4th bhava governs mother, home, land, vehicles, and general domestic comfort; the Chaturthamsha (D4) is examined specifically for fixed property and real-estate fortune.

The 3rd bhava shows younger siblings and courage; the 9th shows elder siblings, father, and fortune more broadly — classical texts read both houses together for the full sibling picture, not the 3rd alone.
The Dwadashamsha (D12) is examined for parents and ancestral lineage specifically — a finer lens than the 4th/9th houses alone for questions about parental welfare and inherited patterns.

The 12th bhava governs foreign residence and life far from one's birthplace; the 9th governs long journeys and fortune connected to distant places. Classical texts read both together for questions of relocation and life abroad, not the 12th in isolation.

Rahu is the planet most consistently associated with foreign lands, unconventional geography, and emigration in classical and modern practice alike; its house placement and dignity are read for the flavour and timing of foreign connection.
The 3rd bhava governs short journeys and everyday travel, distinct from the 9th/12th's longer-distance and foreign-residence significations — a chart can show ease in one register without the other.

The 6th bhava governs open enemies, disputes, and litigation; the 12th governs hidden losses and confinement. A strong 6th lord is classically read as an advantage in contested matters, while a weak or afflicted 6th lord favours settlement over confrontation.

Vipareeta Raja Yoga (a dusthana lord placed in a dusthana) is classically read as turning apparent obstruction into eventual advantage; in litigation contexts this is sometimes cited as a pattern for prevailing after early difficulty, though that is an interpretive extension rather than the yoga's primary classical scope.

The Lagna (ascendant) and its lord govern physical constitution and core temperament — how the self meets and engages with the world; the lord's strength and placement colour confidence, resilience, and self-expression.

The Moon governs the mind and emotional responsiveness — the instinctive, feeling nature beneath the Lagna's outward temperament. Its sign, house, and aspects shape how emotions are processed and expressed.

A Pancha Mahapurusha yoga forms when Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, or Saturn occupies its own or exaltation sign in a kendra from the Lagna; each is classically read as a distinct, well-defined strength — courage, intellect, wisdom, refinement, or discipline respectively — rather than a generic boost.

Kemadruma dosha (no planets in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon, and none conjunct it) is classically read as a tendency toward emotional self-reliance or a sense of isolation — a flag to work with, like any dosha, not a fixed deficiency in someone's character.
A strong 10th lord — exalted, or in its own rashi or navamsha — gives fame and accomplished deeds; the same verse ties this to happiness from the father.
A 10th lord devoid of strength brings obstruction in one's work.
The 10th lord with a benefic, or placed in an auspicious house, gives gain through institutional patronage and through business; the contrary placement gives the contrary result.

Fame is indicated by the Moon in the 10th with the 10th lord in a trine from the 10th and the lagna lord in an angle from the lagna; also by the 11th lord in the 10th while a strong 10th lord receives Jupiter's aspect.
The 10th lord in the 10th makes one skilful in all kinds of work.
The dasha of the 10th lord brings recognition and award from the governing authority — read in a modern chart as institutional recognition, office or promotion.

The 10th bhava is the house of karma — acts and deeds — and carries the father alongside profession; several 10th-lord placements speak to the father rather than to work, so a 10th-house judgement should not be reduced to livelihood alone.

source.location: ch.21 v.2 and ch.24 v.114, pp.137,149 (Santhanam trans.)

references.statement: The 10th lord in the 8th house conjunct Rahu, while generally a difficult combination for professional happiness, is specifically noted as auspicious for the leather trade, life-insurance work, and the mining industry.

Saturn and Mars together with the 10th lord in the 7th house, the house of trade and business, with the 7th lord itself afflicted, is read by one translation as a caution toward illegal or unethical means in trade — a professional-conduct reading of the same combination another translation reads only as personal character. Cite as a trade-conduct caution, never as a character or sexual-conduct verdict.

source.location: ch.23 v.7 (Sharma trans.); cf. ch.21 v.7, p.138 (Santhanam trans.)

references.observance_note: The two translations of this verse diverge: Sharma reads it as a caution about illegal or unethical trade conduct, Santhanam's ch.21 v.7 reads the same combination as a personal-character remark. This app cites the trade-conduct reading only — never as a character or sexual-conduct verdict — and states that the reading is one of two translator interpretations rather than implying the text speaks with one voice.

references.statement: The Sun conjunct Rahu, Mars and Saturn in the 11th house afflicts the Sun as significator of will and self-confidence, and the native fails to complete his professional efforts.
Saturn together with a debilitated planet in the 10th house, with the 10th house's own navamsha also afflicted by a malefic, leaves the native bereft of accomplishment in his actions.

The 10th lord in the 2nd house, well placed, is read as banking, finance, or governmental-authority professions — high officials in banks, finance ministers, or holders of special governmental authority.
The 10th lord in the 3rd house, for a Capricorn ascendant specifically, is read as prompting an engineering profession.
The 10th lord in the 4th house is read as a profession relating to automobiles, building material, agriculture, or dairy.
The 10th lord in the 5th house is read as statesmen, scholars, professors, writers, educationists, or actors — professional distinction through intellectual or creative work.
The 10th lord in the 6th house is read as auspicious specifically for doctors and lawyers; other professions under this placement see more fluctuation and obstacles.
The 10th lord in the 8th house is read as favouring trades in scrap, mineral substances, life-insurance work, or leather goods; other professions under this placement fail badly.
The 6th bhava governs disease, and ulcers or bruises of the body.
The 6th lord in the 6th, the lagna or the 8th indicates ulcers or bruises on the body; the sign falling in the 6th indicates which limb is concerned.

When a karaka or a bhava lord joins the 6th lord or occupies the 6th or 8th, the affliction indicated belongs to the relative that karaka signifies, not to the native — the governing frame of this rule is relatives, not a body-map of the reader.
The 6th lord in the lagna tends to a sickly constitution, alongside prominence and friction with one's own people.
The dasha of the 6th lord brings ill health and trouble from adversaries; the dashas of the 11th and 12th lords likewise carry a susceptibility to disease.

Across the twelve placements of the 6th lord only two speak to sickness; the remainder concern temperament, relationships and expenditure. The 6th lord signifies conflict and outlay at least as much as illness, so not every 6th-lord placement is a health statement.

Where a dasha lord sits by drekkana sets when inside the period its effects are felt — first drekkana at the commencement, second in the middle, third at the end — and retrogradation reverses that order, so the ever-retrograde nodes are always reversed. This is emphasis within the period, never a boundary on it.

A dasha runs favourably when its lord is in the lagna, exalted, in its own sign or a friend's sign at the period's commencement, and adversely when the lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated, or in an inimical sign.

Dignity and placement override a planet's natural benefic or malefic character for its dasha: a malefic exalted and in a good house does not give adverse results, while a benefic debilitated and in an inauspicious house does.

The 2nd and 7th lords are counted among the marakas, but their dashas are not read as distress alone: the 2nd is the house of wealth and a well-placed 2nd lord gives definite gain in its period, and the 7th indicates marriage, so a well-placed 7th lord brings auspicious celebration.
references.observance_note: Stated by the translator against a flat reading of the same chapter's own list. Recorded because reducing a 2nd- or 7th-lord dasha to distress misreads the source.

references.statement: Whether the lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th give adverse results in their dashas is disputed within the text itself: ch.34 states that they do, while the ch.48 commentary holds from practice that they do not when placed in the 3rd, 6th and 11th respectively in their own signs.

source.location: ch.34 and ch.48 commentary, p.466 (Santhanam trans.)

references.observance_note: A genuine intra-text conflict, left unresolved. State which reading is being used rather than implying the text speaks with one voice.

references.statement: The 7th lord placed in the 6th, 8th or 12th weakens the marriage's support and flags the partner's wellbeing as a concern.
A 7th lord endowed with strength and well placed supports the marriage; weak and afflicted, it does not. Strength of the 7th lord is the first thing judged, before any single combination.
The 7th house or its lord conjunct a malefic brings difficulty to the partner and strain to the union.
The Moon in the 7th with an afflicted 7th lord indicates a lack of conjugal ease. The translator adds that the Moon here should be waning — a condition the verse itself does not state.
references.observance_note: The waning-Moon requirement is the translator's gloss, not in the verse. State which reading is used.

references.statement: BPHS gives combinations for the timing of marriage, and the text itself splits them into those that bring it early and those that delay it. The stated ages belong to a period of child betrothal and are not literal ages for a modern reader: they indicate marriage EARLIER or LATER than the reader's own norm, never a specific year of age.
references.observance_note: Ages of 7 to 19 in the source reflect historical child-betrothal norms. Read the combinations as early-versus-delayed relative to the reader's context; never restate an age as a prediction.

references.statement: Venus in the 2nd with its dispositor joined to Mars; the 7th lord in the 12th with the lagna lord in the 7th in navamsha; and the 8th lord in the 7th with Venus in the navamsha lagna are each read as delaying marriage.
The 7th lord in the 7th itself gives happiness in marriage.
The 7th lord in the 8th deprives the native of marital happiness.

Only about half of the 7th lord's twelve placements speak to the marriage at all; the rest concern wealth, siblings and children. The 7th lord signifies partnership and gain through others together, so not every 7th-lord placement is a statement about the spouse.
A strong 5th lord aspected by strong Mercury, Jupiter and Venus indicates many children.

Any one of three conditions on the 5th lord indicates children will come: exaltation, placement in the 2nd/5th/9th from lagna, or conjunction/aspect with Jupiter. The conditions are independently sufficient, not cumulative.

Three or four malefics in the 5th with a debilitated 5th lord flags behavioural challenges in the children; a benefic (including Mercury) placed in the 5th cancels the combination. A flag on tendency, not a verdict on character.
The 5th house tenanted by six planets, its lord in the 12th, with a strong Moon and lagna, indicates adopted issue.

BPHS gives several combinations for the age at which children arrive, and every one of them falls late relative to typical fertility timing. Read as the chart indicating a LATER path to children, never as a literal guaranteed age for a modern reader.
references.observance_note: Specific ages (32, 33, 36, 40) are the source's own figures. State the combination and the direction (delayed), never assert the literal age as a prediction.

references.statement: Roughly half of the 5th lord's twelve placements concern children directly; the rest speak to wealth, siblings, standing and temperament. The 5th lord signifies intelligence, merit and purva-punya as much as progeny, so not every 5th-lord placement is a statement about children.

The 12th lord and 12th house both afflicted by and aspected by malefics indicates movement from country to country; the same combination with benefics instead indicates the native stays within their own country. The two verses are read as a pair, inverted between malefic and benefic association.

A second classical technique for profession, independent of the 10th lord's Rashi placement: the navamsa occupied by the 10th lord names the type of livelihood — for example the Sun's navamsa indicating government or priestly service, Mercury's indicating writing, scholarship or clerical work, Mars's indicating metals, conflict or adventurous trades. Two authors centuries apart both treat the 10th lord as the key career significator, through different vargas.

The 7th house or its lord afflicted by, aspected by, or positioned between malefics brings harm to the marriage. Independently states the same claim as BPHS ch.18 v.16 (bphs18_16_malefic_on_seventh) — two authors, same underlying rule.
A strong, well-placed and unafflicted 7th lord, aspected by Jupiter, brings a marriage with happiness and children. Independently corroborates BPHS ch.18 vv.4-5 (bphs18_4_seventh_lord_strength).

Marriage may occur during the dasha of a planet occupying, aspecting, or owning the 7th house, or when the lagna lord transits into the sign representing the 7th house. A dasha-based marriage-timing technique not offered directly in the BPHS extract.

Jupiter and a well-placed 5th lord, aspected by a benefic or a lord of an auspicious house, assure children; the character of the children follows from the 5th lord's own strength. Independently corroborates BPHS ch.16 vv.12,16 (bphs16_12_many_children, bphs16_16_children_come).

The 5th house in a sign owned by Saturn or Mercury, aspected by or associated with Mandi or Saturn, or a weak 5th lord disconnected from the lords of the 1st and 7th houses, indicates a child by adoption. Independently corroborates BPHS ch.16 v.11 (bphs16_11_adoption).

The birth of a child may occur during the dasha of the lagna lord, the 7th lord, the 5th lord, Jupiter, or a planet aspecting or occupying the 5th house, or when Jupiter transits the sign occupied by the 5th lord. A dasha-based children-timing technique structurally parallel to the marriage-timing rule from the same book.

A strong 2nd-house lord's dasha brings family success, good fortune and eloquence; a strong 7th-house lord's dasha brings new possessions, marital happiness and celebration. Stated as the base verse, not as commentary on a contrary reading -- a direct, independent corroboration of the caveat that the 2nd and 7th lords, though counted among the marakas elsewhere in this text, give gain rather than distress alone when well placed.
A strong, well-placed Jupiter in this 6th/8th-lord-in-lagna configuration tends to protect against illness — a positive constitutional signal, not a caution.

This configuration with Mercury indicates a constitutional tendency toward Pitta/bilious-type sensitivity — digestive and metabolic — read as a susceptibility, not a diagnosis, the same way a dosha is a flag rather than a verdict.
references.observance_note: The verse names the constitutional type (Pitta/bilious) only; the 'digestive and metabolic' body-system gloss reflects standard Ayurvedic dosha-to-system association, not wording stated verbatim in this BPHS verse -- same category of added elaboration as the Kapha clause's convention_dependent treatment above.

references.statement: This configuration with Saturn indicates a constitutional tendency toward Vata/windy-type sensitivity — joints, nerves, mobility — read as a susceptibility, not a diagnosis.
references.observance_note: The verse names the constitutional type (Vata/windy) only; the 'joints, nerves, mobility' body-system gloss reflects standard Ayurvedic dosha-to-system association, not wording stated verbatim in this BPHS verse -- same category of added elaboration as the Kapha clause's convention_dependent treatment above.

references.statement: This configuration with the Moon indicates a constitutional tendency toward Kapha/phlegmatic-type sensitivity — respiratory and fluid balance. Only this clause of the Moon's line is kept; a separate 'danger through water' phrase in the same verse is too ambiguous to state responsibly and is dropped.

source.location: ch.17 v.9-12½ (Moon clause, phlegmatic only), p.115 (Santhanam trans.)

references.observance_note: Only the phlegmatic/Kapha clause is used; the verse's separate water-danger phrase is excluded as too ambiguous to ground responsibly.

references.statement: This configuration with Mars indicates a tendency toward injury, wounds, or accident-proneness — a materially different claim from disease susceptibility, and the direct classical answer to whether a chart shows accident risk.
The 8th lord placed in the lagna indicates a general vulnerability to injury or wounding. The verse's separate clause about religious hostility is unrelated to health and is not carried over.

The 8th lord placed in the 6th house indicates a general susceptibility to illness (unnamed in the verse). The same shloka carries a childhood-danger clause and a separate clause on the closed topic documented for the 8th house generally (see health_kb_bphs_6th_house.md) -- neither is carried over here.
The ascendant lord placed in a sign of Mars or Mercury and aspected by Mercury is classically read as a caution toward the facial area -- worth attending to, not a diagnosis of a specific condition.

Mars or Mercury owning the ascendant and joining the Moon, Rahu or Saturn is classically read as a caution toward skin and immune-system vulnerability -- a signal historically taken seriously enough to warrant particular care, not a named diagnosis. The verse's own named condition is a specific, now-stigmatizing historical term and is deliberately not repeated; the underlying combinatorial signal (skin/immune area, worth checking) is what is kept.
references.observance_note: The verse names a specific historical disease term across three variants (by planet). Reframed to the body-system area the verse itself is organized around, dropping the stigmatizing specific name; this is a deliberate softening, stated so the boundary is visible rather than implied.

references.statement: The lords of the 6th and 8th conjunct the Sun in the ascendant is classically read as a caution toward febrile or inflammatory susceptibility -- general systemic wellbeing worth attending to during flare periods, not a named condition.
references.observance_note: The verse's second term (historically 'tumour', which in period medical English denoted any abnormal swelling, not specifically malignancy) is generalized to inflammatory/swelling susceptibility rather than read as a cancer-specific claim, since the source text does not support that specificity either way.

references.statement: The lords of the 6th and 8th conjunct Ketu in the ascendant is classically read as a caution toward the abdominal/digestive area -- worth attending to, not a named diagnosis.

Saturn with Rahu conjunct the 6th lord and 6th house, or Mars in the 6th with the 6th lord in the 8th, is classically read as flagging childhood as a period warranting extra health vigilance -- a general caution about a life-stage, not a named condition or a specific age.
references.observance_note: The verse states specific ages (6 and 12) tied to specific named illnesses. Neither the age nor the illness name is carried over -- only the life-stage-level flag, for the same reason a marriage or children timing verse's literal age is not restated as a modern prediction: a specific year is a period artifact, and pairing it with a named illness is the clearest case of a medical verdict this corpus holds.

references.statement: The Moon in Sagittarius or Pisces with Jupiter in the 6th, Rahu in the 6th with the ascendant lord in the 8th and Mandi in an angle, or the 6th and 12th lords in exchange, are classically read as flagging youth and young adulthood as a period warranting extra health vigilance -- a general caution, not a named condition or a specific age.
references.observance_note: Same treatment as the childhood entry: the verse's named illnesses and specific ages (19, 22, 26) are not carried over, only the life-stage-level flag.

references.statement: Saturn and the Moon together in the 6th, or Saturn with an inimical planet as the ascendant lord occupies the ascendant, are classically read as flagging midlife and later years as a period warranting extra health vigilance -- a general caution, not a named condition or a specific age.
references.observance_note: Same treatment: the verse's named illnesses and specific ages (45, 59) are not carried over, only the life-stage-level flag.

references.statement: The 2nd lord in the 2nd house, an angle, or a trine from the ascendant promotes wealth; in the 6th, 8th or 12th it indicates decline. A benefic occupying the 2nd house supports wealth, a malefic there works against it.
Jupiter as the 2nd lord placed in the 2nd house, or Jupiter conjunct Mars, indicates wealth.
The 2nd lord in the 11th house while the 11th lord is in the 2nd -- or both lords together in an angle or a trine -- indicates wealth.
The 2nd lord in an angle while the 11th lord occupies a trine from that position, or the 2nd lord aspected by or conjunct Jupiter and Venus, indicates wealth.

The 2nd and 11th lords placed together in the 6th, 8th or 12th house, with a malefic occupying the 2nd, is read as a caution toward financial strain -- worth attending to, not a fixed verdict on the native's means.

The 2nd and 11th lords in the 6th, 8th or 12th together with Mars in the 11th and Rahu in the 2nd indicates financial loss through penalties or fines from an official or governing authority -- read in the modern sense (tax, legal or regulatory loss), per the source commentary's own gloss.
Jupiter in the 11th house, Venus in the 2nd, a benefic in the 12th, and the 2nd lord conjunct a benefic indicates expenditure directed toward religious or charitable purposes.
The 2nd lord conjunct a benefic and placed in a strong divisional-chart dignity indicates wealth acquired without significant effort, extending to the native's family.
The 11th lord in the 11th house, an angle, or a trine from the ascendant indicates many gains; even if combust, an exalted 11th lord still indicates many gains.
The 11th lord in the 2nd house while the 2nd lord is in an angle conjunct Jupiter indicates substantial gains.
The 11th lord in the 3rd house while the 11th house itself is occupied by a benefic indicates a notable gain.
references.observance_note: The verse names a specific age (36th year) and a specific quantity of Nishkas (an archaic gold-coin unit). Both are dropped as unservable false precision -- an obsolete currency figure has no honest modern reading, and a literal age here follows the same softening already applied to marriage's and children's timing verses. Only the chart combination and its general direction (a notable gain) are kept.

references.statement: The 11th lord conjunct a benefic in an angle or a trine indicates a notable gain.
references.observance_note: Age (40th year) and Nishka amount dropped for the same reason as the neighbouring verse (S22.4) -- unservable false precision, not a disputed reading.

references.statement: Jupiter in the 11th house with the Moon in the 2nd and Venus in the 9th indicates a substantial gain.
references.observance_note: Nishka amount dropped for the same reason as S22.4/S22.5 -- an obsolete currency figure has no honest modern reading.

references.statement: Jupiter, Mercury and the Moon together in the 9th house (the 11th-from-the-11th) indicates wealth, provisions, fortune and fine ornaments.
The 11th lord in the ascendant while the ascendant lord is in the 11th house indicates a notable gain.
references.observance_note: Age (33rd year) and Nishka amount dropped for the same reason as S22.4/S22.5/S22.6 -- unservable false precision.

references.statement: The 11th lord in the 2nd house while the 2nd lord is in the 11th indicates abundant fortune accumulating, particularly following marriage.
The 11th lord in the 3rd house while the 3rd lord is in the 11th indicates wealth gained through siblings, along with fine ornaments.

The 11th lord in fall, combust, or in the 6th, 8th or 12th house with a malefic is read as a caution that gains may not come easily despite effort -- a flag on the native's earning tendency, not a fixed verdict.
The 2nd lord in the 2nd house indicates wealth and more than one significant partnership.
The 2nd lord in the 4th house indicates wealth of all kinds; exalted there and conjunct Jupiter, it indicates prosperity comparable to royalty.
The 2nd lord in the 5th house indicates wealth, with the native's children also inclined toward earning.
The 2nd lord in the 6th house conjunct a benefic indicates gain through rivals or competitors; conjunct a malefic instead, it indicates loss through the same.
The 2nd lord in the 8th house indicates abundant land and wealth.
The 2nd lord in the 9th house indicates wealth, diligence and skill.
The 2nd lord in the 11th house indicates wealth of every kind, along with diligence, honour and renown.

The 2nd lord alone in the 12th house generally indicates reduced wealth; the source notes that with two or more favourable planets also present in the 12th, the placement instead indicates considerable wealth.
The 11th lord in the ascendant indicates a native who is prosperous, content, and consistently gaining.
The 11th lord in the 2nd house indicates wealth of every kind along with a charitable disposition.
The 11th lord in the 3rd house indicates skill across undertakings and wealth.
The 11th lord in the 4th house indicates gains through maternal relatives along with happiness from house and land.
The 11th lord in the 7th house indicates gains coming through the spouse's relatives.
The 11th lord in the 9th house indicates good fortune and affluence.
The 11th lord in the 11th house, its own, indicates gains increasing across all undertakings, day by day.
The 11th lord in the 12th house indicates habitual expenditure toward good causes, along with connections abroad.
